notes: EmitterObj C2 (cursor overload): same body as C1 0x86c5ec. Partial for the reason C1 has: the chunk inputs come from the data object, not the cursor words (see 0x86d238)

EmitterObj::LoadAsync: cursor, chunk size (bits*length/8 or 150 ms rounded to frames) and the buffer ring. Partial: the listing's source words for bits per sample and length are not matched to DataObj fields; the port reads the DataObj fields

EmitterObj::Update(float): LoadAsync gate, reset, loop, 3D and DSP calls, fades, source gain and pitch, state moves. Partial: the cursor channel count (the 3D test) is read from the data object, not the cursor words, and the +0x145 flag is a plain byte

VoxEngineInternal::KillEmitter: stamp bump, priority bank removal, CleanUp, data unregister and destruction are written. Missing: the driver call at +0x48 for a DSP source, the release of the source at +0x114, and the pending-release list (+0x6c, mutex +0x74) read by UpdateSources

EmitterObj::Play: body matches the listing (resume fade from sub-state 2 or from 0, sub-state 1). Only the int return is missing: the listing returns the pthread unlock result (Mutex::Unlock tail-calls pthread_mutex_unlock, asm 0x893478); the port's Mutex::Unlock is void

EmitterObj::Pause: body matches the listing (sub-states 1, 2 and 3). Only the int return is missing: the listing returns the pthread unlock result (Mutex::Unlock tail-calls pthread_mutex_unlock, asm 0x893478); the port's Mutex::Unlock is void

EmitterObj::Stop: body matches the listing (sub-states 1 to 3, silent fade when not playing). Only the int return is missing: the listing returns the pthread unlock result (Mutex::Unlock tail-calls pthread_mutex_unlock, asm 0x893478); the port's Mutex::Unlock is void

PriorityBankManager::AddEmitter: admission gate, append for behaviour 3 or room, behaviour 0 eviction of the first entry, behaviours 1 and 2 victim scans (2 keeps an equal-priority fallback). The victim's bank flag is cleared and Stop(0) is called; Stop is ported. Tested in priority_bank_add_emitter_test. The writer of EmitterObj priority_ (+0x2c) is outside this body

VoxUtils::LoadDataSourceFromFileToRAM: opens the file, sizes it, reads it into a VoxAlloc buffer, closes it, hands it to the engine as a RAM source; empty handle on any failure before the hand-off. Partial: the listing's read call has no count argument (port passes the remaining bytes); the engine load call drops the engine and sixth arguments

VoxUtils::LoadDataSourceFromFile: engine path load (kind 1) with the format. Partial: VoxEngine::LoadDataSource is declared on a static facade whose body waits on VoxEngineInternal::LoadDataSource, which is partial (probe and track parameters); the sixth argument is dropped

VoxUtils::LoadDataSourceFromFileAsRAW: loads through LoadDataSourceFromFile then converts. Partial: in the listing the convert call takes the engine singleton where the loaded handle appears expected; the port converts the loaded handle (unconfirmed)

VoxUtils::LoadDataSourceFromFileEx: routes by load flags (0x10000 async, bit 0 RAM, value 2 RAW, else file). Partial: the async call drops the sixth argument and the user value; the dispatch is complete

VoxUtils::LoadDataSourceFromFileAutoDetectDecoder: picks the decoder from the extension (wav 1, ogg 2, mpc 3, vxn 4), else empty handle. Dispatch is complete; the load goes through the partial LoadDataSourceFromFile

VoxUtils::LoadDataSourceFromFileAutoDetectDecoderEx: as AutoDetectDecoder through LoadDataSourceFromFileEx with load flags and user value. Dispatch is complete; the load goes through the partial LoadDataSourceFromFileEx
DecoderCursorInterface::DecodeRef: loads the pointer from the reference and calls vtable slot +0x10 (Decode) with it and the count (asm 0x86fb44). Decode(dst, count) is the same virtual call

mpc_getsize: the listing reads the cursor's +0x04 owner word and calls its vtable slot +0x10 (StreamInterface::Size). Missing: StreamCursorInterface has no +0x04 owner member (StreamMemoryBufferCursor and StreamCFileCursor keep their own), so the port returns 0. Moving the owner into the base would close it

DecoderMPC8Cursor::Decode: buffered copy, decode loop and loop restart follow the listing. Two deviations: (1) on the overrun path the listing passes r1 to the loop-restart seek, but r1 is clobbered by the convert/memcpy call first, so the port seeks to the pre-update position; (2) the port stops when mpc_demux_decode returns 0 samples, the listing calls it again. Demux calls are upstream libmusepack

DecoderMPC8::CreateNewCursor: body ported as the free function vox::CreateDecoderMPC8Cursor (sizeof the 64-bit cursor, placement construct, null on allocation failure). Not installed as the override: that makes decoder_mpc8_test reference the upstream demux functions, which the test does not link

DecoderMSWav D2: parse_pending_ set, the data list's successors are freed (DataNode::DropNodes, 0x870e38, ported), the head is freed and the field cleared. The listing calls DropNodes on the node after the head and frees that node, then the head: the same blocks are freed, in a different order
DecoderMSWav D1: same body as D2 (0x870f7c), verified by a textual diff of the two listings
DecoderMSWav deleting destructor: calls the D1 body, then frees the object. Compiler-generated wrapper of the reconstructed D1

DecoderNativeCursor::ParseFile: full chunk walk (Afmt, Segm, Cues, Grpe, Rule, Plst, Stat, Trsn, Grps; unknown ids skipped). Missing: header body words at +0x0c..+0x17, the Afmt id and size words at +0x1c and +0x20, and the fmt bytes past +0x2f are not stored. Trsn passes the last Stat count where the listing reads a stack slot only Stat writes

DecoderNativeCursor C1: body reproduced (playlist copy, PCM format 1 or IMA format 17 with two states each, track parameters, frame capacity 600*channels*word2/500). Partial only because header_words_ is filled by ParseFile, which is partial (missing header words, see 0x8738bc)
DecoderNativeCursor C2: same body as C1 0x8742f4. Partial for the same reason: header_words_ comes from ParseFile, which is partial (see 0x8738bc)

VoxMSWavSubDecoderIMAADPCM::DecodeBlock: reads one block and decodes it with ImaAdpcmDecodeBlock (ima_adpcm.cpp, tested). Missing: the byte values of AdpcmDecoder::cAdpcmStepSizeTable (89 int16, 178 bytes at .rodata 9509412) and cAdpcmIndexTable (16 bytes at 9509396). The port uses the standard IMA tables, which are not read from the binary (no .so in this checkout, only debug and symbol dumps)

RandomGroup C2 constructor: the listing does not write +0x38 (element count), +0x44 (current index), +0x50 or +0x54. The port sets 0, -1, 0, 0; the -1 at +0x44 is a port default not written by the listing, so it is right only if the caller's storage is left alone
RandomGroup C1 constructor: same body as C2 0x881ad0. Partial for the same reason: the listing leaves +0x38, +0x44, +0x50 and +0x54 to the caller's storage; the port's -1 at +0x44 is a default

SequentialGroup::GetGroupElementPosition: the advance, wrap, cycle and saved-state writes match the listing. Partial: with an empty element vector the listing reads element 0 through a null begin pointer (fault) after writing the state; the port returns -1 with no side effects

RandomGroup::SetToPreviousState: saved values, reinsert pop, tail push, unlink and free match the listing. Partial: with an empty removed list and a positive exclusion window the listing pushes the sentinel's +0x38 word (element count) as the element and adds its weight; the port pushes null and dereferences it

RandomGroup::SetState(RandomGroup&): base copy, scalar fields and element pointers match the listing. Partial: when the removed list is empty and this vector is longer than the source, the listing reads the element-count word after the sentinel as the padding pointer; the port uses null. The surplus relink is kept as the listing writes it

RandomGroup::AddElement: the listing copies the 8-byte element into a new heap block, pushes the copy, updates the count (+0x38), the exclusion window (+0x3c, when the raw window is -1) and the total weight (+0x48), and returns the old total weight. Partial: the port pushes the caller's pointer (native_playlist_walk.cpp passes an owned copy), returns void and keeps no count or weight. Closing it needs the caller to stop copying
